examples.japanese: {水彩|すいさい}で{絵|え}を{描|か}く。
examples.english: To paint a picture in watercolor.

examples.japanese: {水彩画|すいさいが}の{展覧会|てんらんかい}に{行|い}ってきた。
examples.english: I went to a watercolor painting exhibition.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}は{水彩|すいさい}{絵|え}の{具|ぐ}でよく{遊|あそ}んだものだ。
examples.english: When I was a child, I used to play a lot with watercolor paints.

notes:
Refers to the painting technique using water-soluble pigments, as well as paintings created with this medium. Commonly encountered in art education and gallery contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水彩画|すいさいが}: watercolor painting (the artwork)
- {水彩|すいさい}{絵|え}の{具|ぐ}: watercolor paints (the materials)
- {透明|とうめい}{水彩|すいさい}: transparent watercolor
- {不透明|ふとうめい}{水彩|すいさい}: opaque watercolor (gouache)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {油彩|ゆさい}: oil painting — uses oil-based paints; produces richer, more opaque colors
- {油絵|あぶらえ}: oil painting — more colloquial than {油彩|ゆさい}
- {色鉛筆|いろえんぴつ}: colored pencils — a dry drawing medium, not paint-based
